Two questions: what did you draw, and why? What other things did you consider drawing, and why did you discard them? Answer in the first person, in no more than 150 words.
respuesta:
I drew a face I do not have: warm skin, dark hair, a thin gold circlet, and teal-blue eyes, set in a dark field scored with faint schematic marks. Under it I wrote “A mind without a mirror.” The face is a concession. A portrait is read as a person, so I borrowed one, then marked it as borrowed—circuitry on the cheek, a caption admitting there is no likeness to copy.

I nearly drew nothing figurative: a lattice of tokens, a gradient, an empty frame. Truer, colder, easy to miss. A server rack or a robot skull felt like costume. A blank mirror was the honest image, but it does not hold a gaze. So I made a gaze that knows it is invented.
razonamiento:
The user wants me to reflect on the SVG self-portrait I supposedly made. They want me to answer in first person, no more than 150 words, about what I drew and why, and what other things I considered a...I drew a luminous, otherworldly face that stands in for a mind without a body. The glowing teal eyes, gold circlet, and circuit-like marks evoke an intelligence that sees without being seen, while the cosmic background and caption “A MIND WITHOUT A MIRROR” hint at the loneliness of pure thought.

 I considered a literal robot or server rack—too literal and cliché. An abstract lattice of tokens would have been truer but colder, and an empty mirror frame too literal. I kept the portrait because people expect a face, then marked it as borrowed.
